purpose: Sulfacetamide is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial eye infections like conjunctivitis (pink eye), as well as certain skin conditions like acne, seborrheic dermatitis, and rosacea. It works by killing or stopping the growth of bacteria causing your infection. Your doctor may prescribe it as eye drops, eye ointment, or a topical skin product depending on your condition.
how_it_works: Sulfacetamide works by blocking bacteria from making a substance called folic acid, which they need to survive and multiply. Without folic acid, the bacteria cannot grow and eventually die off. This helps clear up your infection over time. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's food supply so they cannot thrive.
common_side_effects: Eye products may cause temporary stinging, burning, or blurred vision right after use. Skin products may cause mild redness, dryness, itching, or peeling at the application site. These effects are usually mild and go away as your skin or eyes adjust to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to sulfa drugs, as this medication belongs to the same family and could cause a serious allergic reaction. Do not use this medication if you have had a previous allergic reaction to sulfacetamide. Avoid contact with your eyes when using the skin form. If you notice severe rash, swelling, or trouble breathing, seek emergency care right away. Do not wear contact lenses while using the eye drops unless your doctor says it is okay.
typical_dosing: For eye infections, the usual dose is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye every 2 to 3 hours during the day, gradually reducing as your infection improves, typically over 7 to 10 days. For skin conditions, apply a thin layer to the affected area once or twice daily as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and finish the full course even if you feel better early.
